**Date:** {{< meta display-date >}}  
**From:** {{< meta from-address >}}  
**Manuscript Location:** {{< meta manuscript-location >}}  

My dear [Henry](../persons.html#184)
[Mr Steward](../persons.html#1680) has written at last.

He says two very nice girls [Mildred Luckett](../persons.html#906) and [Kate Brown](../persons.html#212) will be ready at Christmas, so I am writing to him to engage one of them, and she can talk it over with [A.

Diddams](../persons.html#1681) who can tell her all about the place.[^2]
He also gives me a list of ex pupil teachers who could keep school after the 1st of October till the mistress is ready.

They all have homes near at hand and I think we can get one of them.
[Amy Bateman](../persons.html#783) is going to Winchester tomorrow, so I am sending her the names and asking her to enquire.

Your affectionate

C M Yonge

[^1]: The letter must date between the arrival of the Bowleses in Otterbourne in October 1892 and the marriage of Amy Jones-Bateman in August 1894.

[^2]: Mildred Luckett (b.

Dalston 1871/2) and Kate H.

Brown (b.

Salisbury 1871/2) were both pupils at the Salisbury Diocesan Training School in 1891, learning to be teachers.
